title: Trump’s Risky Strategy to Blockade Iran’s Blockade

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·荣森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店打碟的黑胶唱片时代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去上班，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼带来的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: It is a high-stakes game of blockade chicken.
sentences.zh: 这是一场高风险的封锁博弈。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: asserts control over the Strait of Hormuz.
sentences.zh: 宣称对霍尔木兹海峡拥有控制权。

sentences.en: Iran, for its part, threatens retaliation.
sentences.zh: 而伊朗方面则威胁要进行报复。

sentences.en: For the past two days, the United States has enforced a risky naval blockade of Iran designed to end the war on American terMs.
sentences.zh: 过去两天里，美国对伊朗实施了一项高风险的海上封锁，旨在以美国的条件结束这场战争。

sentences.en: So what are we doing?
sentences.zh: 那么我们到底在做什么？

sentences.en: We're blockading the ports in Iran where they get oil and gas shipments.
sentences.zh: 我们正在封锁伊朗获取石油和天然气运输的港口。

sentences.en: Without oil and gas money, Iran has no economy.
sentences.zh: 没有了油气收入，伊朗的经济就瘫痪了。

sentences.en: Today, a look at the strategy behind the blockade, the dangers that it poses, and whether or not it's actually working.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们来审视一下这项封锁背后的战略、它所带来的危险，以及它是否真的奏效。

sentences.en: We can't let a country blackmail or extort the world, because that's what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 我们不能让一个国家勒索或敲诈全世界，因为这正是他们正在做的事。

sentences.en: They're really blackmailing the world.
sentences.zh: 他们确实在勒索全世界。

sentences.en: We're not going to let that happen.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不会让这种情况发生。

sentences.en: I spoke with White House correspondent David Sanger, energy reporter Rebecca Elliott, and military correspondent Eric Schmidt.
sentences.zh: 我采访了白宫记者大卫·桑格、能源记者丽贝卡·埃利奥特和军事记者埃里克·施密特。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, April 15th.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月15日，星期三。

sentences.en: David, Rebecca, Eric, thank you for joining us for this roundtable discussion.
sentences.zh: 大卫、丽贝卡、埃里克，感谢你们参加我们的圆桌讨论。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Great to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: David, I want to start with where the idea for this blockade comes from.
sentences.zh: 大卫，我想先从这项封锁计划的起源谈起。

sentences.en: It emerges right after Iran basically sent Vice President J.D.
sentences.zh: 它出现的时间点，就在伊朗基本上把副总统J.D.

sentences.en: Vance packing, sends him home from negotiations in Pakistan with no deal.
sentences.zh: 万斯打发走，让他空手从巴基斯坦的谈判中回家之后。

sentences.en: And suddenly, the Trump administration is confronting a pretty messy situation, a ceasefire without Iran letting go of control over the Strait of Hormuz, this huge,
sentences.zh: 突然间，特朗普政府面临着一个相当棘手的局面：伊朗在停火的同时，并没有放弃对霍尔木兹海峡的控制权，这是一个巨大的、

sentences.en: important shipping channel.
sentences.zh: 重要的航运通道。

sentences.en: And so that seems to be where this blockade begins, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这似乎就是封锁开始的地方，对吧？

sentences.en: You're absolutely right, Michael,
sentences.zh: 你说得完全正确，迈克尔，

sentences.en: that it seemed intolerable to the administration that you could end this war or move toward an end of it with the Iranians exercising control over who gets through the strait.
sentences.zh: 对政府来说，如果伊朗能控制谁可以通过海峡，那么战争的结束或走向结束就显得令人无法容忍。

sentences.en: Because through the whole 47 years of the Islamic Revolutionary government in place since 1979, they basically let all traffic go through without tolls.
sentences.zh: 因为在1979年伊斯兰革命政府执政的47年里，他们基本上让所有船只免费通行。

sentences.en: And now, all of a sudden, they managed to stop traffic.
sentences.zh: 而现在，他们突然设法阻止了交通。

sentences.en: They managed to declare that there would be tolls.
sentences.zh: 他们设法宣布要征收过路费。

sentences.en: We're still trying to figure out how much they actually collected.
sentences.zh: 我们还在试图弄清楚他们到底收了多少钱。

sentences.en: Literally, when we say tolls, literally like the one you pass on the highway.
sentences.zh: 说真的，当我们说“过路费”时，指的就是你在高速公路上经过的那种收费。

sentences.en: Yeah, $2 million.
sentences.zh: 没错，200万美元。

sentences.en: Imagine every time your easy pass went through, it put $2 million on your credit card, right?
sentences.zh: 想象一下，每次你的自动缴费卡通过时，信用卡上就会被扣掉200万美元，对吧？

sentences.en: This was not a situation the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这不是美国

sentences.en: could live with.
sentences.zh: 能够接受的局面。

sentences.en: So what the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以美国

sentences.en: Navy needed to do was reverse the dynamic, make sure that it wasn't the Iranians who were controlling traffic through the strait, but that it was the U.S.
sentences.zh: 海军需要做的是扭转这种态势，确保控制海峡交通的不是伊朗人，而是美国

sentences.en: Navy that was.
sentences.zh: 海军。

sentences.en: And that sounds like a fairly straightforward process given the size of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 考虑到美国

sentences.en: Navy.
sentences.zh: 海军的规模，这听起来是一个相当直接的过程。

sentences.en: But in fact, it turns out it's looking like it will be pretty complicated to execute.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，执行起来似乎会非常复杂。

sentences.en: So, Eric, just define this pretty brute force military concept of a naval blockade because it's its own act of aggression.
sentences.zh: 那么，埃里克，请定义一下这种相当粗暴的军事概念——海上封锁，因为它本身就是一种侵略行为。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: By definition, a blockade is an act of war.
sentences.zh: 根据定义，封锁就是战争行为。

sentences.en: And what it means is one country is basically going to use its military might, its forces, to block the transit of ships from other countries.
sentences.zh: 它的意思是，一个国家基本上要利用其军事力量和军队，来阻断其他国家的船只通行。

sentences.en: That can either be through the threat of force or actual boarding of ships and seizing them.
sentences.zh: 这可以通过武力威胁，或者实际登船扣押来实现。

sentences.en: And in this case,
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，

sentences.en: the United States Navy has shown up with some 10,000 sailors aboard more than a dozen warships from aircraft carriers to destroyers to the ships that carry marines.
sentences.zh: 美国海军出动了约1万名水兵，随行的有十几艘军舰，从航空母舰到驱逐舰，再到搭载海军陆战队的舰船。

sentences.en: And they're essentially parked outside of the Strait of Hormuz,
sentences.zh: 他们基本上停泊在霍尔木兹海峡外，

sentences.en: basically waiting for any ships to come either from the Persian Gulf or trying to get from where they are in the Arabian Sea into the Gulf itself.
sentences.zh: 等待着任何从波斯湾出来的船只，或者试图从阿拉伯海进入海湾的船只。

sentences.en: Basically, the idea is to strangle Iran's economy, but specifically, Rebecca, to strangle its oil.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这个想法是为了扼杀伊朗的经济，但具体来说，丽贝卡，是为了扼杀它的石油。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And what's so interesting is that Iran has been able to maintain oil going through the strait in a way that its neighbors have not.
sentences.zh: 最有趣的是，伊朗一直能够以其邻国无法做到的方式，维持石油通过海峡运输。

sentences.en: So it's exerting this control over the waterway by attacks and threats of attacks.
sentences.zh: 所以它通过攻击和攻击威胁，对这条水道施加了控制。

sentences.en: So the vast majority of the oil that has been getting through has come from Iran.
sentences.zh: 因此，绝大多数通过海峡的石油都来自伊朗。

sentences.en: So it's continuing Iran to make money from oil to, in a sense, I assume, fund its own war efforts.
sentences.zh: 所以伊朗继续通过石油赚钱，在某种意义上，我假设，是为了资助它自己的战争努力。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: And just to add to Rebecca's point here, it's not only the overall Iranian economy that's dependent on this revenue.
sentences.zh: 补充一点丽贝卡的观点，不仅仅是整个伊朗经济依赖于这种收入。

sentences.en: It's particularly the government and within that, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps,
sentences.zh: 特别是政府，以及其中的伊斯兰革命卫队，

sentences.en: which gets almost all of its revenue and thus its ability to pursue the war from oil exports.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎所有的收入，以及因此进行的战争能力，都来自石油出口。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And just to be sure, we're all on the same page here.
sentences.zh: 为了确保我们达成共识，

sentences.en: Is the goal ultimately to wrest back control of the strait or is the goal to create a blockade that would bring Iran back to the negotiating table so that this war actually never reignites?
sentences.zh: 最终目标是为了夺回海峡的控制权，还是为了制造一场封锁，迫使伊朗回到谈判桌前，从而让这场战争永远不再重燃？

sentences.en: Well, as I understand it, it's really both.
sentences.zh: 嗯，据我所知，两者兼而有之。

sentences.en: I mean, they don't want to live in a world in which the Iranians step out at any moment to control the strait.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们不想生活在一个伊朗人随时可以跳出来控制海峡的世界里。

sentences.en: If that's the case, then the U.S.
sentences.zh: 如果是这样的话，那么美国

sentences.en: has to be prepared for a lengthy presence around the Strait of Hormuz.
sentences.zh: 就必须准备好在霍尔木兹海峡周边进行长期驻扎。

sentences.en: But the real goal here is to get the Iranians to move in the negotiations.
sentences.zh: 但这里的真正目标是让伊朗人在谈判中做出让步。

sentences.en: Remember, this got announced right after Vice President Vance left Islamabad fundamentally empty-handed.
sentences.zh: 记住，这是在万斯副总统从伊斯兰堡空手而归后宣布的。

sentences.en: We've since learned that they are in a pretty high-stakes negotiation on a number of points.
sentences.zh: 我们后来了解到，他们在多个议题上进行了相当高风险的谈判。

sentences.en: But the biggest difference is whether or not Iran has to give up its nuclear stockpiles and whether it's got to agree to give up all enrichment of uranium.
sentences.zh: 但最大的分歧在于伊朗是否必须放弃其核储备，以及是否必须同意放弃所有铀浓缩活动。

sentences.en: But whatever it is, the strait and control over it is the leverage President Trump's trying to exercise here.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，海峡及其控制权是特朗普总统试图在这里行使的筹码。

sentences.en: Okay, a final question about the blockade before we get to how it's actually going so far,
sentences.zh: 好的，在讨论目前进展如何之前，关于封锁的最后一个问题是，

sentences.en: which is if you're the president and you're deciding to operationalize this theoretical blockade,
sentences.zh: 如果你是总统，决定实施这一理论上的封锁，

sentences.en: what are the risks that you're assessing as you're thinking about making this real?
sentences.zh: 当你考虑将其变为现实时，你评估的风险是什么？

sentences.en: I put that to all three of you.
sentences.zh: 我把这个问题抛给你们三位。

sentences.en: What kind of blowback, boomeranging, can you expect as you imagine suddenly creating this naval barrier around the strait?
sentences.zh: 当你想象突然在海峡周围建立这种海上屏障时，你会预料到什么样的反弹或回旋镖效应？

sentences.en: Well, one major risk, of course, is that the IRGC and Iran itself lashes out.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一个主要的风险当然是伊朗革命卫队和伊朗本身会进行反击。

sentences.en: They have threatened to attack these U.S.
sentences.zh: 他们已经威胁要攻击这些美国

sentences.en: Navy ships.
sentences.zh: 海军舰艇。

sentences.en: And so you could have a major escalation of the fighting again based over the ships coming into the strait or even standing back outside.
sentences.zh: 所以，基于进入海峡的船只，甚至是在外围驻守的船只，你可能会再次引发战斗的重大升级。

sentences.en: So that would be one major risk that the president would have to weigh.
sentences.zh: 所以这将是总统必须权衡的一个重大风险。

sentences.en: There's a second one I can think of, and I'm sure Rebecca's got a long list as well.
sentences.zh: 我还能想到第二个，我相信丽贝卡也有一长串清单。

sentences.en: It's China.
sentences.zh: 那就是中国。

sentences.en: So 90 percent of the oil that Iran ships out is headed to China.
sentences.zh: 伊朗出口的石油中，90%是运往中国的。

sentences.en: Much of it is on Chinese-crewed, Chinese-flagged ships.
sentences.zh: 其中大部分是在中国船员驾驶、悬挂中国国旗的船只上。

sentences.en: The president's supposed to go to Beijing in about four weeks,
sentences.zh: 总统大约四周后要去北京，

sentences.en: and what he was hoping was going to be this meeting all about sort of a new detente between China and the United States.
sentences.zh: 他原本希望这次会晤能成为中美之间某种新缓和关系的契机。

sentences.en: There were supposed to be trade deals and security understandings and so forth.
sentences.zh: 原本应该有贸易协议、安全谅解等等。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, what's looming over it?
sentences.zh: 而突然之间，什么笼罩在这一切之上？

sentences.en: Whether or not these Chinese ships that pick up their oil in Iran get turned back by the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这些在伊朗装载石油的中国船只是否会被美国

sentences.en: Navy.
sentences.zh: 海军拦截。

sentences.en: That is not the kind of scene they want to be confronting, especially at a moment when there are reports, as Eric and others have reported in the Times,
sentences.zh: 那不是他们想面对的场景，尤其是在埃里克和其他人在《时报》报道称，

sentences.en: that the Chinese have been considering aiding the Iranians with some kind of arMs.
sentences.zh: 中国人一直在考虑向伊朗人提供某种武器的时候。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: A simple, efficient way to really piss off your superpower adversary is to start to systematically deprive them of oil.
sentences.zh: 激怒超级大国对手的一个简单而有效的方法，就是开始系统性地剥夺他们的石油。

sentences.en: Rebecca, any risks you want to identify?
sentences.zh: 丽贝卡，你还有什么想指出的风险吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I'd say a third big category of risk is that Iran responds by restarting attacks on energy infrastructure throughout the Persian Gulf.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想第三大类风险是伊朗通过重启对波斯湾各地能源基础设施的攻击来做出回应。

sentences.en: And that is one that carries really long-term risks for the global energy system and the global economy.
sentences.zh: 这对全球能源系统和全球经济来说，确实带有长期风险。

sentences.en: Because as you do more damage to the region's infrastructure, prevent refineries from operating, you risk taking energy offline for a long period of time.
sentences.zh: 因为当你对该地区的基础设施造成更多破坏，阻止炼油厂运营时，你就冒着长期切断能源供应的风险。

sentences.en: And already,
sentences.zh: 而且已经，

sentences.en: the International Energy Agency has estimated that more than 80 energy sites in the region have been damaged and that bringing production back to pre-war levels could take up to two years.
sentences.zh: 国际能源署估计，该地区已有超过80个能源设施受损，将产量恢复到战前水平可能需要长达两年时间。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So, this blockade has now gone from strategic theory to reality.
sentences.zh: 所以，这场封锁现在已经从战略理论变成了现实。

sentences.en: So, let's turn to what it's looked like over the past 48 hours or so, and whether it's working for the U.S.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们转向过去48小时左右的情况，看看它对美国是否有效，

sentences.en: or creating a bunch of strategic boomeranging blowbacks that were perhaps unintended but now problematic.
sentences.zh: 还是造成了一系列可能是无意但现在却很麻烦的战略反弹。

sentences.en: Eric, to start, can you describe the blockade as it now stands around the strait?
sentences.zh: 埃里克，首先，你能描述一下目前海峡周围的封锁状态吗？

sentences.en: So, as I mentioned before, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前提到的，美国

sentences.en: Navy is positioned outside the Strait of Hormuz, kind of waiting for any ships bound for Iranian ports.
sentences.zh: 海军部署在霍尔木兹海峡外，等待着任何前往伊朗港口的船只。

sentences.en: So, what President Trump is calling a blockade is really more of a quarantine.
sentences.zh: 所以，特朗普总统所说的封锁，实际上更像是一种检疫。

sentences.en: They're monitoring these ships using drones, using other open source information about where these ships are coming from or where they're going to.
sentences.zh: 他们利用无人机和其他关于这些船只来源或去向的开源信息来监控它们。

sentences.en: And if there's a suspect ship, they can get on the radio and basically call and determine if that's a ship that they might need to board.
sentences.zh: 如果有一艘可疑船只，他们可以通过无线电联系，确定是否需要登船检查。

sentences.en: And if it got to that point, they could actually send boarding parties aboard.
sentences.zh: 如果到了那一步，他们实际上可以派出登船小组。

sentences.en: These would be Marines or specially trained Navy personnel, could be Navy SEALs, they could arrive by boat,
sentences.zh: 这些将是海军陆战队或受过专门训练的海军人员，可能是海豹突击队，他们可以通过小艇到达，

sentences.en: they could come by helicopter and fast rope down onto these ships to inspect the cargo.
sentences.zh: 他们可以通过直升机快速绳降到这些船上检查货物。

sentences.en: This would really be only if the ships continue apace.
sentences.zh: 这真的只有在船只继续前进的情况下才会发生。

sentences.en: One of the reasons why you have this blockade or quarantine is really to set a deterrent.
sentences.zh: 你进行这种封锁或检疫的原因之一，实际上是为了建立威慑。

sentences.en: The idea that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: Navy is out there and do the shipping companies whose cargo is moving, do they really want to have the United States seize this cargo?
sentences.zh: 海军在那里，那些货物正在运输的航运公司，他们真的想让美国扣押这些货物吗？

sentences.en: Do they really want to challenge the United States?
sentences.zh: 他们真的想挑战美国吗？

sentences.en: I think most of the hundreds of ships that are already on scene, whether they're inside the Persian Gulf or outside, are kind of staying put.
sentences.zh: 我认为已经在现场的数百艘船只中，无论是在波斯湾内还是外，大多都处于观望状态。

sentences.en: And what we're now waiting for to see if there's any Iranian-backed ships that dare them.
sentences.zh: 我们现在正在等待，看看是否有任何伊朗支持的船只敢于挑战他们。

sentences.en: Well, so far, are any ships carrying Iranian oil, the thing the U.S.
sentences.zh: 那么，到目前为止，是否有任何运载伊朗石油的船只——即美国

sentences.en: blockade is meant to stop, are any of those ships getting through the strait since this blockade started?

sentences.en: So let's talk about what's happening to everyone else in the world when it comes to this blockade.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们来谈谈这场封锁对世界上其他人意味着什么。

sentences.en: So far, as you all just established before the break, the Iranian oil seems to be bottled up because of this blockade.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，正如你们刚才在休息前所确定的那样，由于这场封锁，伊朗的石油似乎被困住了。

sentences.en: A success strategically if you're the U.S.
sentences.zh: 如果你是美国，这在战略上是一次成功。

sentences.en: trying to disrupt the Iranian economy and get the Iranians back to the negotiating table to end this war.
sentences.zh: 试图扰乱伊朗经济，迫使伊朗人回到谈判桌前结束这场战争。

sentences.en: But if you are the UAE, if you are the United States, if you're Russia, what does this blockade mean for you so far, Eric?
sentences.zh: 但如果你是阿联酋，如果你是美国，如果你是俄罗斯，埃里克，这场封锁到目前为止对你意味着什么？

sentences.en: Do we have any intelligence about whether cargo ships are seeing the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我们是否有任何情报显示货船是否将美国的

sentences.en: blockade as a safety net that lets them get through the strait?
sentences.zh: 封锁视为一种安全网，让他们能够通过海峡？

sentences.en: Well, just before coming on the program, a U.S.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就在上节目之前，一位美国

sentences.en: official told me that as many as 20 commercial vessels have now been able to transit through the strait in the first 24 hours or so.
sentences.zh: 官员告诉我，在过去24小时左右的时间里，已经有多达20艘商船成功通过了海峡。

sentences.en: Now, the official didn't describe exactly what kind of ships, but it's assumed this is a combination of tankers, of cargo ships, and other things.
sentences.zh: 这位官员没有具体描述是什么类型的船只，但推测这是油轮、货船和其他船只的组合。

sentences.en: But we really need more detail to see if this is an early indication of a broader stream, like as Rebecca said,

sentences.en: of shippers who are now more confident that they can run the gauntlet that they weren't before.
sentences.zh: 那些货运商现在更有信心去闯关了，而他们之前并没有这种信心。

sentences.en: Or if this is just a momentary spurt of getting through with the U.S.
sentences.zh: 或者这只是在美国海军

sentences.en: Navy standing by that really doesn't have a long-term effect.
sentences.zh: 待命的情况下，短暂的通行爆发，实际上并没有长期的影响。

sentences.en: Rebecca,
sentences.zh: 丽贝卡，

sentences.en: what are your sources telling you about the trepidation level of the captains of these ships and the companies that own them and have to pay the insurance levels that they're paying now to try to go through the strait?
sentences.zh: 你的消息来源对于这些船只的船长以及拥有这些船只、且必须支付目前高昂保险费才能尝试通过海峡的公司，他们的担忧程度如何？

sentences.en: I would say it's very high.
sentences.zh: 我会说非常高。

sentences.en: And increasingly, the people I speak with are starting to ask not what is it going to take to reopen the strait,
sentences.zh: 而且，我交谈的人越来越多地开始问的不是“需要什么条件才能重新开放海峡”，

sentences.en: but will the strait ever go back to the way it was before the war when there was free passage, no toll, and relatively little risk of being attacked?
sentences.zh: 而是“海峡还能回到战前那种自由通行、没有过路费、且几乎没有被攻击风险的状态吗？”

sentences.en: And many people think probably not.
sentences.zh: 许多人认为可能回不去了。

sentences.en: Let's now turn to that question, basically, the long-term future of the strait and what it's going to look like.
sentences.zh: 现在让我们转向那个问题，基本上就是海峡的长期未来及其形态。

sentences.en: Is it going to be something that, over time, the Iranians just control, perhaps in a peace deal?
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，这会变成伊朗控制的事物吗，也许是在和平协议中？

sentences.en: Or does this become some sort of a joint operation over time?
sentences.zh: 还是说这会逐渐变成某种联合行动？

sentences.en: Does the strait ever get restored to its pre-war operations?
sentences.zh: 海峡能恢复到战前的运作状态吗？

sentences.en: Can that genie ever be put back into the bottle, David?
sentences.zh: 大卫，那个魔鬼还能被重新关回瓶子里吗？

sentences.en: So I'm with Rebecca.
sentences.zh: 所以我同意丽贝卡的看法。

sentences.en: I don't think that you're going to see it go back to the way it was anytime soon because the Iranians have discovered this kind of superpower they have.
sentences.zh: 我不认为短期内你会看到它恢复原状，因为伊朗人已经发现了他们拥有的这种“超级力量”。

sentences.en: They had never before tried to control the strait, and suddenly they discovered that after much of their military has been destroyed, they have the ability,
sentences.zh: 他们以前从未尝试过控制海峡，突然间他们发现，在大部分军事力量被摧毁后，他们有能力，

sentences.en: just by dropping a few mines or threatening ships with shoulder-fired missiles, to basically bottle up everything that's in the Persian Gulf.
sentences.zh: 仅仅通过投放几枚水雷或用肩扛式导弹威胁船只，就能基本上封锁波斯湾内的一切。

sentences.en: So we have heard a couple of proposals.
sentences.zh: 所以我们听到了一些提议。

sentences.en: At one point, President Trump just briefly suggested that maybe it would be run by him and the new Ayatollah Khamenei.
sentences.zh: 有一次，特朗普总统曾简短地建议，也许可以由他和新任最高领袖哈梅内伊来管理。

sentences.en: That would be a business partnership I'd like to go cover.
sentences.zh: 那将是一场我想去报道的商业伙伴关系。

sentences.en: There have been more serious proposals about creating a kind of international consortium that not only monitored what was going through, but maybe charged and divided up the tolls.
sentences.zh: 还有一些更严肃的提议，即建立一个国际财团，不仅监控通过的船只，甚至可能收取并分配过路费。

sentences.en: You could imagine Iran would be a part of that, Oman, which is straight across the other side of the strait, the United States, which would be providing security.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象伊朗会参与其中，还有海峡对岸的阿曼，以及提供安全保障的美国。

sentences.en: And then you could imagine bringing in any number of countries that are dependent on what's traveling through the strait, starting with China, maybe with India, and, of course,
sentences.zh: 然后你可以想象引入任何数量依赖海峡航运的国家，从中国开始，也许还有印度，当然，

sentences.en: the Europeans.
sentences.zh: 还有欧洲国家。

sentences.en: Now,
sentences.zh: 现在，

sentences.en: that would require a level of international cooperation and diplomatic sharing of power that so far the Trump administration has not shown a great interest in around the world.
sentences.zh: 那将需要一种国际合作和外交权力共享，而特朗普政府到目前为止在世界范围内并没有表现出太大的兴趣。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so this would be a really interesting test to building an international coalition.
sentences.zh: 所以这将是建立国际联盟的一个非常有趣的考验。

sentences.en: So, David and Rebecca, what you seem to both be saying is that at the end of this conflict,
sentences.zh: 那么，大卫和丽贝卡，你们两人似乎都在说，在这场冲突结束时，

sentences.en: the strait will never again be like the Atlantic Ocean or like the Pacific Ocean and be a free international waterway in which commerce occurs pretty much unimpeded and free.
sentences.zh: 海峡将永远不会再像大西洋或太平洋那样，成为一个商业往来几乎畅通无阻且自由的国际水道了。

sentences.en: Never say never, but that is certainly something that more and more people are facing at this moment.
sentences.zh: 永远别说永远，但这确实是越来越多的人此刻正在面对的事实。

sentences.en: And when we're talking about the oil market and energy demand, that leads in a few different directions.
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论石油市场和能源需求时，这会引向几个不同的方向。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: How do you start to plan around a world where maybe the strait is told to a degree that's not tolerable?
sentences.zh: 你如何开始规划一个海峡收费高到令人无法忍受的世界？

sentences.en: Doesn't that require a whole new level of alternatives?
sentences.zh: 这难道不需要一个全新的替代方案吗？

sentences.en: I would divide it into three general buckets.
sentences.zh: 我会把它分为三个大类。

sentences.en: One is the possibility of building more alternative routes from Gulf countries to world markets that get around the strait of Hormuz.
sentences.zh: 一是建设更多从海湾国家通往世界市场、绕过霍尔木兹海峡的替代路线的可能性。

sentences.en: We already have a couple of those options in Saudi Arabia and the UAE, and they have been helping to get oil out to a very big degree.
sentences.zh: 我们已经在沙特阿拉伯和阿联酋有了几个这样的选择，它们在很大程度上帮助了石油出口。

sentences.en: Are those shipping alternatives or pipelines?
sentences.zh: 那是航运替代方案还是管道？

sentences.en: Pipelines.
sentences.zh: 管道。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Now, that is complicated as well.
sentences.zh: 现在，这也很复杂。

sentences.en: There are only a certain number of countries that are able to get oil from one coast to another without running across another country's territory.
sentences.zh: 只有少数几个国家能够在不经过别国领土的情况下将石油从一个海岸运到另一个海岸。

sentences.en: So then you get into the cooperation conversation again.
sentences.zh: 所以这就又回到了合作的话题上。

sentences.en: That's one bucket.
sentences.zh: 这是第一类。

sentences.en: Another bucket is, does this increase demand for oil elsewhere in the world that you can get without running the risk of going through the strait?
sentences.zh: 第二类是，这是否会增加世界其他地区对石油的需求，而这些石油无需冒着通过海峡的风险就能获得？

sentences.en: And the third is, whenever oil is more expensive, it makes alternatives more attractive.
sentences.zh: 第三是，每当石油价格上涨，就会使替代能源更具吸引力。

sentences.en: And those alternatives include nuclear energy, solar power, batteries.
sentences.zh: 这些替代能源包括核能、太阳能、电池。

sentences.en: And we're already seeing many of those conversations pick up around the world.
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到世界各地关于这些话题的讨论在增加。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So the entire world of energy and energy infrastructure could end up changing because of this war and, to a degree, because of this blockade.
sentences.zh: 所以整个能源和能源基础设施的世界最终可能会因为这场战争，在某种程度上因为这场封锁而改变。

sentences.en: And that could end up long outlasting the conflict itself.
sentences.zh: 而且这可能会在冲突本身结束后持续很长时间。

sentences.en: In the long term, Michael, I think that's exactly what could happen.
sentences.zh: 从长远来看，迈克尔，我认为这正是可能发生的事情。

sentences.en: And, of course, it's been different wars, different conflicts that have shaped our energy status in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 当然，过去不同的战争和冲突塑造了我们的能源地位。

sentences.en: But the way I try to think about this in the short term is that we are now entering a contest over which country, the United States or Iran,
sentences.zh: 但我尝试从短期来看，我们现在进入了一场竞赛，看哪个国家——美国还是伊朗，

sentences.en: can endure the pain of this blockade over the next few months.
sentences.zh: 能在未来几个月里忍受这场封锁带来的痛苦。

sentences.en: The Iranians are betting that it's Trump who is going to have to back off.
sentences.zh: 伊朗人押注特朗普将不得不退缩。

sentences.en: And Iran knows this.
sentences.zh: 伊朗知道这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, their leadership in Internet memes taunts Trump about gas prices.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们的领导层在互联网模因中嘲讽特朗普的汽油价格。

sentences.en: In fact, their lead negotiator, the Speaker of the Iranian Parliament, basically said as he left Islamabad, you could be nostalgic for $5 or $6 a gallon gas.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们的首席谈判代表，伊朗议会议长，在离开伊斯兰堡时基本上说，你们可能会怀念每加仑5或6美元的汽油。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: has a different bet, which is what they failed to do militarily in 38 or 39 days of war, they can finish off economically by cutting off Iran's main source of revenue,
sentences.zh: 有不同的赌注，那就是他们在38或39天的战争中没能通过军事手段做到的，他们可以通过切断伊朗的主要收入来源来在经济上完成，

sentences.en: by specifically cutting off the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, and that they will, in the end, come back to the negotiating table and, as President Trump put it, cry uncle,
sentences.zh: 特别是通过切断伊斯兰革命卫队的资金，最终他们会回到谈判桌前，正如特朗普总统所说，认输求饶，

sentences.en: say, we're going to do whatever you want to do.
sentences.zh: 说，我们愿意做你们想做的任何事。

sentences.en: So far, that hasn't happened.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，这种情况还没有发生。

sentences.en: But the president is testing to see where that point is.
sentences.zh: 但总统正在测试那个临界点在哪里。

sentences.en: And the fact of the matter is, if anybody tells you they know which side is not going to be able to withstand the pain first, I'm not sure I'd believe them yet.
sentences.zh: 事实是，如果有人告诉你他们知道哪一方会先无法承受痛苦，我还不确定是否会相信他们。

sentences.en: But, Eric, final question to you, how sustainable is this blockade if it lasts for a while?
sentences.zh: 但是，埃里克，最后一个问题，如果这场封锁持续一段时间，它的可持续性如何？

sentences.en: The next negotiation session between the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国和伊朗之间的下一次谈判会议在周四，但两国在所有主要症结上的分歧，

sentences.en: and Iran is on Thursday, but the gap between the two countries on all the major sticking points,
sentences.zh: 无论是核计划还是以色列在黎巴嫩持续的战争，依然巨大。

sentences.en: whether that's the nuclear program or Israel's ongoing war in Lebanon, remains enormous.
sentences.zh: 如果美国持续要求封锁，它的可持续性如何？

sentences.en: How sustainable is the blockade if it keeps being required by the U.S.?
sentences.zh: 嗯，五角大楼表示，只要总统需要，他们就能维持这场封锁。

sentences.en: Well, the Pentagon has said that it can sustain this blockade as long as the president needs to.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，这将以牺牲军队在世界其他地方必须执行的任务为代价。

sentences.en: The problem is it would come at a cost of what the military has to do elsewhere around the world.
sentences.zh: 它已经抽调了在印太地区急需的舰船和弹药，以可能对抗中国，处理朝鲜的冲突。

sentences.en: It has already drawn away ships and munitions that are badly needed in the Indo-Pacific to possibly counter China, to deal with North Korea in a conflict there.
